subject: Consent grace window & staging rollback plan for Summit West capture
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@quantforge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Consent grace window & staging rollback plan for Summit West capture

Jamie —

Quick note as we prep for the Summit West badge-capture run this week. Two items to align on before on-site:

1) Consent grace window: we plan to surface a 14-day post-capture grace window for attendees who opt out after the event. During this window leads will be held in a quarantine HubSpot list ("SummitWest-Quarantine-14d") and will not sync to SFDC until either consent is confirmed or the grace period expires.

2) Staging rollback plan: if we detect mapping regressions during the first hour of live capture, we will trigger an automated rollback that flips the HubSpot-to-SFDC sync to the previous mapping and pauses new syncs for 30 minutes while ops investigates. The ops runbook and rollback script are attached for your review (rollback_script.sh).

Attached: consent_text_v2.docx (updated language with explicit opt-out), hubspot_field_mapping.csv (staging mapping), rollback_script.sh (ops script stub).

Ask: can you confirm that holding leads in a quarantined HubSpot list for 14 days and preventing SFDC sync during that window is acceptable to QuantForge procurement and their reps? Also: will disabling the SFDC sync for 30 minutes be problematic for your SDR routing?

If you want a short call to walk through the run order I have availability 11:00–12:00 PT today.

Thanks,

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Field Marketing Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Park <jamie@quantforge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consent grace window & staging rollback plan for Summit West capture

Hannah —

Thanks for the run-through and attachments. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I pull procurement in: 

- Holding leads in a quarantine list for 14 days is fine from a data-retention/consent POV, but our SDRs source leads from the SFDC "New-Inbound" queue. During the 30-minute pause will the leads still be visible to SDRs in HubSpot? We need to avoid duplicating outreach if the lead is later un-quarantined.

- If a rollback happens and mappings revert, will that create duplicate contacts in SFDC or will the script be mapping by external ID? The mapping CSV you attached looks like it uses email as the unique key but I want to confirm.

Happy to do a quick call at 11:15 PT. Looping in procurement once we confirm the behavior.

Best,
Jamie
Director, Events & Partnerships
QuantForge

> 
> Quick note as we prep for the Summit West badge-capture run this week. Two items to align on before on-site: [truncated]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@quantforge.com>, procurement@quantforge.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consent grace window & staging rollback plan for Summit West capture

Jamie — Thanks, great questions. Short answers up front, details below:

- SDR visibility: leads in the quarantine list will not be pushed to SFDC or the "New-Inbound" queue while quarantined. They will remain visible in HubSpot but will be tagged with "quarantine:true" and a suppression flag that prevents workflow enrollment. That prevents duplicate outreach.

- De-dupes on rollback: rollback_script.sh is ID-aware. It uses our external_lead_id (hashed badge id) to reconcile records; mapping by email is a fallback. We included logic to avoid creating a second contact if an external ID matches. Full logic is in the script comments in the attachment.

Detailed run order (key checkpoints):
- T-1h: Ops enables "staging-mapping" in HubSpot (hubspot_field_mapping.csv).
- Live start: real-time capture writes to HubSpot list "SummitWest-Staging".
- On first anomaly (more than 0.8% field-mismatch rate for 15 minutes): ops toggles the "pause-sync" flag — this triggers rollback_script.sh to revert to last-known-good mapping and pauses outbound syncs for 30 minutes.
- T+30m: If rollback cleared, ops re-enables sync and resumes normal routing; if not, escalation to Platform Eng (Ben) for manual intervention.

Action items:
- Jamie: confirm procurement is good with 14-day quarantine and suppressed SDR workflow.
- Ben: please confirm platform eng is on standby 11:30–12:30 PT day-of (I've CC'd Ben).
- Marissa/Laura: ops to validate rollback script in staging before 18:00 PT today and confirm checksum of hubspot_field_mapping.csv.

Attachment references: consent_text_v2.docx (legal approved language), hubspot_field_mapping.csv (column order matters: external_lead_id,email,first_name,last_name,company,consent_flag,source), rollback_script.sh (bash stub).

I'll join the 11:15 PT call.

—Hannah
Head of Field Marketing Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consent grace window & staging rollback plan for Summit West capture

Looping in ops notes — ops can run the rollback script but we have two asks before we go live: 

1) Please confirm we have a pre-flight test that exercises the external_lead_id branch (not email fallback). I will run a synthetic capture tonight against staging to validate.
2) HubSpot dedupe workflows: if a reverted mapping changes a contact's primary company field, that can trigger our dedupe automation and merge contacts unexpectedly. Recommend disabling the dedupe-for-30m job during the rollback window.

Ben — can you confirm Platform Eng can temporarily disable the dedupe job as part of the rollback runbook? If not, we need an alternative approach (tag-and-hold).

Marissa
Sr. Events Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Consent grace window & staging rollback plan for Summit West capture — final confirmation

Jamie / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick turn. Procurement sign-off received (docuSign link below) with one minor ask: they want a log entry for each quarantine release event (who released it and timestamp). We'll add that to the runbook.

Ben confirmed Platform Eng will pause the HubSpot dedupe workflow during the rollback window and will stand by 11:30–12:30 PT day-of. Marissa validated the pre-flight synthetic test; checksum matched for mapping.csv.

Final decisions: 
- Quarantine window: 14 days, leads suppressed from SFDC and SDR workflows while in quarantine.
- Rollback behavior: revert to last-known-good mapping using external_lead_id; pause outgoing sync for 30 minutes; disable dedupe job for that 30-minute window.
- Audit: add quarantine-release log entry to runbook (required by procurement).

Links: HubSpot company record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/7890
DocuSign (procurement sign-off): https://app.docusign.com/documents/ABCDEF

If nobody objects I'll mark this as approved and trigger the staging smoke test tonight at 20:00 PT. Please reply with a single-line ACK if you're good.

Thanks — Hannah
Head of Field Marketing Operations
Redwood Inference
